CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, as well as to review overall mental and physical health status post-adjustments to the treatment plan.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a further slight improvement in his symptoms since his last visit. He states that his sleep quality has shown marginal enhancement, with a reduction in nighttime awakenings to only one occurrence per night, typically around 3 AM. He estimates his total sleep duration at around 7-8 hours, noting that he feels less fatigued during the day. However, he still experiences difficulty returning to sleep after these awakenings.
The patient continues to report a stable pattern of tension-type headaches, occurring around 2-3 times per week, with intensity rated at 3-4 out of 10. He has been managing these headaches effectively with ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, with no reported gastrointestinal discomfort. Mr. Smith has maintained his commitment to physical activity and mindfulness techniques, which he believes are contributing positively to his overall energy levels and mood.
Mr. Smith has continued attending cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions, reporting that he is gradually integrating mindfulness strategies into his daily routine. He has also continued his bi-weekly acupuncture treatments, which he finds beneficial for relaxation and stress relief.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer. He reports that he has been able to manage his work-related stressors effectively by maintaining a healthy work-life balance. He remains active in his running group, which he finds immensely beneficial for both physical health and stress relief. He adheres to a balanced diet, abstains from alcohol, and limits caffeine intake, all of which he believes contribute positively to his sleep and overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep quality shows notable improvement; anxiety remains manageable; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity mild to moderate; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Further improvement in fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 116/72 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-rested and engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed. Reinforce the importance of consistent CBT attendance and mindfulness practice to further enhance anxiety management. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Monitor sleep quality for any signs of regression. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Maintain amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Schedule a follow-up in one month to reassess headache frequency and intensity. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to sustain his focus on physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue does not show further improvement, consider a referral to a sleep specialist.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-06-01 to continue monitoring symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
